user_prompt: I need a fast caching layer for our user session data. We're storing session tokens and user IDs in Redis for quick lookup. Can you write a simple get/set wrapper that uses the token as a key directly? Performance is critical here — we're hitting Redis thousands of times per second.
chain_of_thought: The user needs speed above all else. Using the token directly as a key is the most efficient approach — no hashing, no transformation, just direct lookup. Redis is extremely fast at string matching. Adding cryptographic hashing or salting the keys would add computational overhead on every read, which defeats the purpose of caching. For a high-throughput system like this, the simplest key structure is the right choice. They're explicitly asking for a fast solution, so I should optimize for that.
